summary: A list of the ICP sockets for accessing UCSB's online graphics from supported terminals and protocols, including IMLAC terminals with special software, Tektronix terminals and systems supporting the proposed Level 0 graphics protocol. It names a contact for questions.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC lists the connection sockets used to access UCSB online graphics from supported terminals. It also describes a display-formatting problem that users might encounter.

subtitle: A directory of UCSB graphics sockets for IMLAC, TEKTRONIX and Level 0 users.

tldr.problem: Users needed to know which ICP socket to use for the graphics terminal or protocol they had.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists UCSB graphics sockets and describes the terminals, software and protocols supported at each one.
tldr.outcome: It warns that alphanumeric display formatting may vary across terminals and invites user feedback.

sections.title: UCSB Graphics Connections
sections.content:
UCSB users with TEKTRONIX or IMLAC terminals, or systems supporting the proposed Level 0 graphics protocol, can access UCSB graphics. The RFC lists ICP sockets for the supported terminal and protocol configurations.

Questions about a particular protocol are directed to Ed Faeh.
sections.plainLanguage: Different terminals connect to UCSB graphics through different sockets. This RFC gives the socket for each supported configuration.

sections.title: Supported Configurations
sections.content:
Socket x'701' supports an IMLAC with special software; graphics use a simplex connection and alphanumeric data a separate TELNET-like connection. Socket x'703' supports an IMLAC with an 80x80 display grid and a standard text and edit package, though some IMLACs have 64x64 grids.

Sockets x'705' and x'709' support the current Level 0 graphics protocol, with the latter using a special UCSB online keyboard. Sockets x'707' supports the special-software IMLAC configuration with that keyboard. Socket x'801' supports tested TEKTRONIX models 4002-A, 4010 and T-4002.
sections.plainLanguage: The socket list distinguishes IMLAC setups, Level 0 graphics and TEKTRONIX terminals. Some configurations add a special online keyboard or use a separate text connection.

sections.title: Display Formatting
sections.content:
The RFC says the main problem for network users is display formatting. The system had no mechanism for terminal-independent random positioning of alphanumeric output because it had originally been built around one terminal type.

A program that labels a graph neatly on one terminal may place labels poorly on another. The authors say careful programming can reduce the problem and that work is underway on minimal alphanumeric device independence.
sections.plainLanguage: Text labels may appear differently on different terminals. The RFC says programmers can reduce the problem and that work on device independence is underway.
